z.$description:
Layering: a system-wide invariant (what covers what), not geometry. The
family declares the order; the values only have to preserve it. Before this
it was five magic numbers in five files: ArenaMenu and ArenaTooltip both sat at 900,
so a tooltip on a menu item resolved by DOM order rather than by design;
Dialog and ArenaConfirmDialog both sat at 1000, and ArenaConfirmDialog opens from a
Dialog, so it worked only by accident of mount order; ArenaToast, the one thing
that must float above everything, declared nothing at all. The order, least
to most interruptible: nav < skip < sheet < dropdown < tooltip < modal <
modal-nested < palette < onboarding < toast.

nav.$description: Fixed page navigation: a bottom bar, a sticky top bar. Arena draws one of these, ArenaBottomNav, and the slot is not there for it: it is there because the invariant is system-wide and a consumer's own shell is part of the system, so a host's sticky header and Arena's bar interleave with Arena's overlays by design rather than by DOM order. That was the reason before any component carried it and it is the reason still; what changed is only that the set of things standing on this step is no longer empty. Below dropdown, so an ArenaMenu opened from the bar covers it rather than resolving by DOM order, which is the failure this family was created to end. Anything drawn against this slot also reads --pad-safe-bottom, in contracts/design/environment.css, and --layout-bar for its own height

skip.$description: The skip link, while it holds focus. It is the one thing on the page that must cover the furniture it exists to bypass: a link that lands under a sticky header is a link nobody can read, and equal numbers resolve by DOM order, which puts the header on top because the skip link is deliberately first in the document. So it is above nav and no higher: everything from sheet upward is a surface that has taken the interaction, and a skip link floating over a modal is a route out of a trap that is meant to hold

sheet.$description: A non-modal panel anchored to an edge: a cart, a filter drawer, a detail pane that leaves the page usable behind it. Arena draws one of these, ArenaSheet, and the slot exists for the same reason nav does: a host's own edge panel stands beside it on the same step. Above nav, because a sheet that slides over a fixed bar and lands under it is the failure; below dropdown, because an ArenaMenu opened from inside the sheet belongs over it. It is NOT modal: a panel that takes the whole interaction is an ArenaDialog, which is two slots higher and has a scrim to say so

dropdown.$description: ArenaMenu's panel: a dropdown anchored to its trigger

tooltip.$description: above dropdown, so a tooltip on a menu item wins

modal-nested.$description: ArenaConfirmDialog, which opens from an ArenaDialog

onboarding.$description: the coachmark and the scrim beneath it: one slot, two uses. The scrim takes the slot and the coachmark is drawn inside it, so the two are separated by containment rather than by a second number; nothing else on the page may sit between them, which is what a single slot means here

toast.$description: floats above everything, including onboarding: a transient notice raised by an action taken inside a dialog must stay visible
